mainTopic: נזיר: amounts for liability, separate liability for grape products, and whether there is מלקות for a לאו שבכללות
overview: The גמרא first explains why the תנא קמא and רבי עקיבא in the משנה disagree about how much a נזיר must eat or drink to be liable. A ברייתא then teaches that fresh grapes and dried grapes each bring their own liability. From there it builds a rule for the whole תורה: one kind of food with two names brings two liabilities, and this includes new wine and grapes. אביי and רבא then argue over how many sets of מלקות a נזיר gets for eating a grape seed or skin. Their argument turns on whether there is מלקות for a לאו שבכללות. רב פפא challenges אביי from a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר counts only five sets of מלקות. The גמרא tries to answer that the list is incomplete, then tests and rejects that answer. רבינא then points out a real omission, and רב פפא concludes that the ברייתא never gave a number at all. A new challenge to this begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next one.

steps.title: Why the two opinions disagree about the amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about eating a כזית of grapes. It explains that the תנא קמא keeps normal amounts for drinking, while רבי עקיבא makes every נזיר prohibition a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a נזיר is liable only once he eats an olive-sized amount of grapes. The תנא קמא does not treat all the נזיר prohibitions like drinking, so each keeps its usual amount. רבי עקיבא learns from the פסוק 'fresh or dried grapes he shall not eat' that, just as eating is a כזית, every נזיר prohibition is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and then explains the reasoning behind the two opinions there about how much a נזיר must consume to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives each נזיר prohibition its normal amount: a כזית for food and a רביעית for drink. רבי עקיבא sees the word 'eat' in the פסוק as setting one amount, a כזית, for all the נזיר prohibitions, including wine.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-sized amount, the standard amount for eating
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
Does not compare or liken
The prohibitions a נזיר must keep
Drinking

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying wine is food. He is saying that for a נזיר, even drinking is measured with the eating amount, a כזית.

phrases.english: he eats an olive-bulk of the grapes, etc.
The first tanna does not liken
them, all the prohibitions of a nazir, to drinking,
And Rabbi Akiva: since it is written
"Nor shall he eat fresh grapes or dried,"
just as eating is an olive-bulk,
so too all the prohibitions are an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא לָא מְדַמֵּי לְהוֹן לְכׇל אִיסּוּרֵי נָזִיר לִשְׁתִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the משנה and explaining its dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא keeps the usual amounts for each prohibition. רבי עקיבא sets a כזית for all נזיר prohibitions, learned from the word 'eat' in the פסוק.

steps.title: Fresh and dried grapes each bring their own liability
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about separate liability. It brings a ברייתא showing that the פסוק makes the נזיר liable for each item on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he is liable for wine by itself, and so on. The Rabbis taught: 'fresh or dried grapes he shall not eat' comes to make him liable for this one by itself and for that one by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and supports it with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק as giving separate liability for fresh grapes and for dried grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this teaching, a person might think the נזיר is liable only if he eats all the listed grape products together. The ברייתא shows that each one listed is its own prohibition, so eating just one is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself, on its own
The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
Fresh and dried grapes (raisins)

phrases.english: And he is liable for wine by itself, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. Some versions have these bracketed words and some don't.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Nor shall he eat fresh grapes or dried,"
to make him liable for this by itself
and for that by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה, a new topic.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that the נזיר is liable for each grape product separately

steps.title: A rule for the whole תורה: one kind with two names
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא turns the grape case into a general rule. When one kind of food has two names, each name brings its own liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here you learn about all the prohibitions in the תורה. Grapes are one kind with two names, fresh and dried, and he is liable for each by itself. So too, anything that is one kind with two names brings liability for each by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא takes the lesson about fresh and dried grapes and makes it a rule for every prohibition in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh and dried grapes are the same fruit, yet the תורה names them separately and gives separate liability. So the deciding factor is the separate name, not a different kind. Wherever the תורה uses two names for one kind, there are two liabilities.

keyTerms.meaning: From here you derive; turns one case into a general rule
One kind or species
Two names

steps.whatToRemember: One kind with two names means two separate liabilities. This rule applies to all prohibitions in the תורה, not only to a נזיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a general tool for counting how many prohibitions a person broke when he ate one food that goes by different names.

phrases.english: From here you derive
for all the prohibitions in the Torah:
just as here, where it is one kind,
and they are two names,
phrases.notes: The two names are 'fresh' and 'dried' grapes.

phrases.english: and he is liable for this by itself
and for that by itself;
so too, anything that is one kind
and they are two names,
he is liable for this by itself
and for that by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אַתָּה דָּן לְכׇל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the ברייתא's grape lesson into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever one kind has two names, there is separate liability for each name.

steps.title: The rule includes new wine and grapes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says what the general rule adds: new wine and grapes bring separate liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to include new wine and grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names a practical case that the two-names rule covers: fresh grape juice and grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh juice is really just grapes in liquid form, so it might seem to be the same item. Because it has a different name, 'wine', it brings its own liability, separate from eating grapes.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to bring in an extra case
New wine, fresh grape juice
Grapes (Aramaic)

phrases.english: To include new wine and grapes.
phrases.notes: 'New wine' means fresh juice that has not fermented yet, so it is still very close to the grapes themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general rule from step 3 to a specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New wine and grapes count as two names, so each brings separate liability.

steps.title: אביי: extra lashes for the general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a נזיר who eats a seed or a skin gets two sets of מלקות, and one who eats both gets three.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: if he ate a grape seed, he gets lashes twice. If he ate a grape skin, he gets lashes twice. If he ate a seed and a skin, he gets lashes three times.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי counts how many sets of מלקות a נזיר gets for eating grape seeds and skins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item has its own specific prohibition, and there is also one general prohibition on anything from the vine. אביי gives lashes for the general one too. That makes two for one item, and three for both, since the general prohibition is counted only once.

keyTerms.meaning: Grape seed
Grape skin
Receives lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If he ate a grape seed, he is flogged twice.
phrases.notes: One set is for the seed itself. The other is for the general prohibition 'anything made from the grapevine' (במדבר 6:4).

phrases.english: If he ate a grape skin, he is flogged twice.
If he ate a grape seed and a grape skin, he is flogged three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about counting מלקות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is מלקות for the general vine prohibition in addition to the specific one.

steps.title: רבא: no lashes for a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees: there is only one set of מלקות, because there is no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: he gets lashes only once, because one does not get lashes for a general prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues with אביי and says the נזיר gets only one set of lashes for the seed or the skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition on 'anything from the vine' covers many items in one לאו, which makes it a לאו שבכללות. רבא holds there is no מלקות for that kind of לאו, so only the specific prohibition counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A general prohibition that covers many items or cases in one 'don't'
He receives lashes only once

steps.whatToRemember: אביי gives extra מלקות for the general vine prohibition. רבא does not, because there is no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות.

phrases.english: Rava said:
He is flogged only once,
because one is not flogged for a general prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה אֶלָּא אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's count in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות, so the נזיר gets only one set of lashes.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges אביי from רבי אליעזר's count of five
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר counts five sets of מלקות for a נזיר who ate and drank many grape products. If אביי is right, it should be six.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected. רבי אליעזר says: a נזיר who drinks wine all day is liable only once. If people warned him 'Don't drink! Don't drink!' and he kept drinking, he is liable for each one. If he ate fresh grapes, dried grapes, seeds and skins, and squeezed a cluster and drank, he gets five sets of מלקות. If אביי is right, he should get six, with one more for ״מכל אשר יעשה״.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא uses a ברייתא to attack אביי's ruling. אביי said the general לאו ״מכל אשר יעשה״ adds its own set of מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר counts five sets of מלקות: fresh grapes, dried grapes, seeds, skins and wine. Under אביי's view there should be a sixth set for the general לאו. Since the ברייתא says five, it seems to agree with רבא that a לאו שבכללות brings no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection from an earlier source
A warning given before a sin. Each separate warning followed by a new act can bring separate liability
Grape seeds and grape skins
He receives מלקות (lashes)
If so (if your view is right)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised an objection:
phrases.notes: He is objecting to אביי, who said the general לאו adds an extra set of מלקות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן כׇּל הַיּוֹם
phrases.english: A nazir who was drinking wine all day
is liable for only one [set of lashes].
If they said to him: "Do not drink," "Do not drink,"
phrases.notes: These are witnesses warning him again and again before each drink.

phrases.english: and he kept drinking,
he is liable for each and every one.
If he ate fresh grapes and dried ones,
seeds and skins,
and squeezed a cluster of grapes and drank,
he receives lashes five times.
If so,
let him receive lashes six times,
one for "anything that is made."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's ruling from Step 5 and seems to support רבא in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that the general לאו ״מכל אשר יעשה״ brings its own set of מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives an exact count of five. If the general לאו added a set, the count would have to be six.

steps.title: The list is not complete
steps.stepSummary: The answer for אביי: רבי אליעזר taught some items and left others out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught some and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. It says the ברייתא's list was never meant to include everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the list is only partial, leaving out ״מכל אשר יעשה״ proves nothing. אביי's sixth set of מלקות can be real even though the ברייתא did not mention it.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught and left out. A list in a ברייתא or משנה does not have to include every case

phrases.english: He taught and left some out.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count of five looked like a full and exact total.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list is partial, so the missing sixth set is not a problem for אביי.

steps.title: What else did he leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for another missing item. A list does not leave out just one thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What else did he leave out, that we can say he left out this one too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer of תנא ושייר. It asks for a second item that the ברייתא skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule behind this question: we only say 'he left things out' if we can find at least one other missing item. A list that is missing only one item looks deliberate.

keyTerms.meaning: What else did he leave out, that he left this out? It asks for another missing item

steps.confusionAlert: תנא ושייר does not work alone. The גמרא almost always demands a second missing item before accepting it.

phrases.english: What else did he leave out, that he left this out?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Another item missing from רבי אליעזר's list.

steps.title: He also left out "He shall not break his word"
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא also left out the לאו of ״לא יחל דברו״.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left out ״לא יחל דברו״, 'he shall not break his word'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names a second missing item. A נזיר who breaks his vow also breaks the general לאו against breaking one's word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״לא יחל דברו״ is also missing, then two items are missing. That would make the list truly partial and keep אביי's answer standing.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not break his word. The לאו against breaking a vow

phrases.english: He left out "He shall not break his word."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא also omitted ״לא יחל דברו״.

steps.title: That one does not count as left out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. רבי אליעזר only lists things special to a נזיר, and ״לא יחל דברו״ applies to all vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is the reason, it is not really a leaving out. He only lists things that are not found anywhere else, and ״לא יחל דברו״ is found by all vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. ״לא יחל דברו״ was never supposed to be on this list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only לאוין that belong to נזירות. ״לא יחל דברו״ belongs to vows in general, so skipping it was on purpose and is not a real omission. That leaves ״מכל אשר יעשה״ as the only missing item, so רב פפא's challenge to אביי comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: A true omission, something that should have been listed but was not
In another place (it applies elsewhere too)
Vows in general

phrases.english: If it is because of that one,
it is not a real leaving out,
because when he teaches, he teaches things
that are not found in another place,
phrases.notes: He means things that apply only to a נזיר and to nobody else.

phrases.english: and "He shall not break his word" is found with vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם הַאי לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 10, which brings back the קשיא of Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects ״לא יחל דברו״ as the second omission, so the defense of תנא ושייר is weakened.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא only lists לאוין special to נזיר, so a general vow לאו was never meant to be on the list.

steps.title: רבינא: the in-between parts are missing too
steps.stepSummary: רבינא from פרזקיא points out that the ברייתא also leaves out the parts between the seed and the skin. The count of five cannot be a full total.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא from פרזקיא said to רב אשי: but he also left out the in-between parts!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא notices another item missing from רבי אליעזר's list. He shows that the list is clearly not complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ״מחרצנים ועד זג״ also includes what lies between the seed and the skin, and that brings its own liability. Since the ברייתא skips it, its 'five' cannot be an exact total. So the count was never strong evidence against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: The in-between parts of the grape, between the seed and the skin

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא מִפַּרְזִקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Ravina from Parzakya said to Rav Ashi:
But he left out the in-between parts!
phrases.notes: These are the parts between the seed and the skin. The פסוק says "from seeds to skin," which includes what lies between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in Step 11 by showing a real omission in the list, which undercuts the count of five used in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the count of five in the ברייתא is a complete total.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The in-between parts also bring liability but are not counted, so the list is not exact.

steps.title: רב פפא: no number five was taught
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא takes back his challenge. The ברייתא never really said 'five'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: the ברייתא did not teach anything about five.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא, who first raised the challenge, now says the number five is not part of the ברייתא at all. The ברייתא just lists items that bring מלקות, without giving a total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the number five, nothing shows that the ברייתא denies a sixth set of מלקות. So the ברייתא is no longer a proof against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not taught at all

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's new answer is that the ברייתא of רבי אליעזר gives no exact count, so it does not disprove אביי. The very next step (״והא״) starts to challenge this claim.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Nothing about "five" was taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא לָא תַּנְיָא מִידֵּי חָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבינא's point from Step 12 to remove the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gave an exact count of five sets of מלקות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא gives no number, so it cannot rule out אביי's sixth set.

steps.title: A new challenge begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with 'But surely...' to start a new challenge, which continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to bring a new difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״והא״ usually opens a challenge from a known source. The challenge itself is stated on the next amud, so for now the learner only needs to know that a new objection is starting.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely... A word that opens a challenge

phrases.english: But surely...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to רב פפא's answer in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the ברייתא did not say 'five' (the challenge continues on the next amud).
